outlier.evidence: Final ratings 6 (iK1S), 5 (wxwg), 4 (vkHd), 6 (F2Td). Before the rebuttal the panel split two against two: iK1S and F2Td at 6, vkHd at 4 and wxwg at 4 or lower ('I raise my score to 5'). No single rating stands apart. Reviewer_vkHd's 4 is the floor, and the AC copied its wording, but it is not isolated.

checkable_claims.claim: The paper has just two myopic baselines and one non-myopic baseline.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 6.1 compares only EIC and PESC (lines 272-273), plus the authors' own SAA_CMAES variant on P3 (lines 282-283). Section 6.2 compares only the rollout method of [1] (lines 289-291).

checkable_claims.claim: All results except 2-OPT-C in the rollout comparison come from another paper, so hyperparameters may differ.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 292-293: 'As code was unavailable for this rollout algorithm, we extract experimental data from [1] and replicate their experimental setup'. The Figure 4 caption says the rollout lines are extracted from Figure 3 of [1].

checkable_claims.claim: The paper claims all BO methods are myopic, which is misleading given UCB and Thompson sampling.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 37-38 limit the claim to the listed constrained BO methods and name the exceptions [1, 14]. Lines 41-42 cite non-myopic unconstrained work [15-19]. UCB and Thompson sampling do not solve the multi-step dynamic program, as the authors replied.

checkable_claims.claim: Line 66 says the method beats the rollout method of [1] in high-dimensional problems, but nothing tests this.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 65-67 make the claim. The only test problems are P1-P3 from [1] (lines 269-271), and no experiment varies the dimension. The camera-ready weakens the claim to 'relatively higher-dimensional problems'.

checkable_claims.claim: The number of experiment repetitions is not in the paper.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 6 and the Figure 3 caption give no replication count; line 271 defers the set-up to the supplement. The authors' answer (150 and 500 replications) points to Appendix A.1.

checkable_claims.claim: The line-220 claim to be the first to use the likelihood ratio method for a BO gradient estimator is contradicted by [17, Section 3.2].
checkable_claims.evidence: The claim is at lines 220-221, and [17] is Wu & Frazier 2019, which is not in the files. The authors replied that [17] uses importance sampling only for variance reduction. The camera-ready narrows the claim to 'the first to demonstrate the benefits' and adds that sentence about [17].

rebuttal.evidence: Only Reviewer_wxwg edited its review (2021-09-01): 'as the authors could clarify some of my concerns during the rebuttal, I raise my score to 5'. The authors' 2021-09-02 reply thanks it for raising. iK1S, vkHd and F2Td never edited, and no reviewer posted on the forum. The authors' 2021-08-11 responses gave a portfolio-optimization experiment (best feasible annualized return 7.08% for 2-OPT-C against 6.60% for EIC and 6.54% for PESC after 30 evaluations, 50 replications). Their 2021-09-02 posts added robot pushing and ADMMBO, NEI, ALBO and random search on P1-P3. These posts came after wxwg's edit, and no reviewer edited after them.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: Clarifications moved wxwg to 5, but its text still says the method 'is not sufficiently evaluated on real-data problems'. Reviewer_F2Td called real-world experiments its 'only concern', received one on 2021-08-11, and did not react. iK1S (confidence 5) did not react to the answers on [17], random search and IECI, and vkHd did not react to the answers on motivation, baselines and Thompson sampling. The AC reports that after 'more than a few communications' no reviewer would champion the paper.

ac.evidence: Split reviews, mean 5.25, no rating above 6. The meta-review says 'none of reviewers are willing to champion this work'. Its requirement, 'It is required to include 1-3 real benchmarks which ideally arise out of motivating applications, more baselines, and ablation studies', copies Reviewer_vkHd's review word for word. It does not mention the portfolio, robot-pushing or new-baseline results that the rebuttal supplied.

main_reasons_for_decision: All four reviewers judged the evaluation too thin: three synthetic problems from [1], two myopic baselines, rollout curves copied from [1]
No rating above 6 after the rebuttal; the two 6s (iK1S, F2Td) never reacted, so the AC found no champion
The AC required real benchmarks, more baselines and ablations in vkHd's words and gave no credit to the rebuttal-period experiments

outlier.evidence: Final ratings 7 (HPhn), 7 (Strq), 6 (uDRU), 5 (8KpE); no isolated rating. The one score below threshold, Reviewer_8KpE's 5, comes from the most thorough review in B (about 6 hours, many specific questions, post-rebuttal follow-ups).

inattentive_reviews.evidence: 2 hours, confidence 3. Its summary says the method 'utilizes reparameterization trick to optimize the acquisition function', but the abstract (lines 18-19) says the estimator 'does not use the reparameterization trick'. It asks how constraints enter because '2-OPT-C doesn't involve constraint function g at all', but line 164 contains the probability-of-feasibility term. Its main text still says the paper 'cannot be accepted in the current form', yet it rose to 6 because it was 'impressed by the amount of work'.

3 hours, confidence 3, math not carefully checked. A 7 on a short review that names one weakness (only three test functions) and says 'The construction of the unbiases estimator is a little bit hard to follow, but I think I understood the overall idea'. Its post-rebuttal note is one sentence.

checkable_claims.claim: The method utilizes the reparameterization trick to optimize the acquisition function.
checkable_claims.evidence: Abstract lines 18-19: the gradient estimator 'does not use the reparameterization trick'. Section 4 explains why reparameterization fails with constraints, and Section 5 replaces it with a likelihood-ratio estimator.

checkable_claims.claim: 2-OPT-C does not involve the constraint function g at all.
checkable_claims.evidence: Line 164: alpha contains PF(mu_1^c(x2), sigma_1^c(x2)^2), the posterior probability of feasibility from the GP on g. f1* (line 149) is the best feasible value, so it also depends on g at X1.

checkable_claims.claim: Assumption 1, needed for Theorem 1, is only in the appendix.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 252-255: 'Both a detailed set of regularity conditions (Assumption 1) and the proof are provided in the supplement.'
Lines 269-271: P1, P2 and P3 from [1] are the only benchmark problems.

checkable_claims.claim: The main paper does not describe the three benchmark problems or define the median utility gap.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 269-277 name P1-P3 and report the 'utility gap' without describing either; both are deferred to the supplement.

checkable_claims.claim: The argument that [1] needs an extremely large amount of computation (lines 50-52) is not well supported.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 303-308: the code of [1] was unavailable, so the paper cites [17]'s timing for an unconstrained rollout and a 'private communication'. No timing of [1] itself is reported.

checkable_claims.claim: Wu & Frazier 2019 already uses importance sampling in a related context, so the work is incremental.
checkable_claims.evidence: The submission says it builds on [17] (lines 74-77). The camera-ready concedes that [17] 'coincidentally also uses importance sampling', as a variance-reduction technique rather than for gradient estimation.

rebuttal.evidence: HPhn edited 2021-08-26: 'increased my score by one unit. Congrats on the convincing responses and promising test case results' (6 to 7). Strq edited 2021-08-27: 'I think adding this example to the paper would make it considerably strongger'; the authors' 2021-09-02 reply thanks it for raising the rating (to 7). uDRU edited 2021-09-02: 'I am quite impressed by the amount of work authors have completed during the rebuttal phase ... I will increase my score to 6'. 8KpE edited 2021-08-30 with follow-up questions and states no change (5). The portfolio experiment came on 2021-08-10/11; robot pushing and the new baselines came on 2021-09-01/02. No reviewer posted on the forum.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: The portfolio experiment convinced HPhn and Strq. uDRU credited the volume of work, not a fix to the clarity problems it named. 8KpE was not convinced: it asked what the risk constraint is, how results change if it is relaxed, why existing BO of risk measures would not do better, and whether a simple EIC change that explores infeasible points would match 2-OPT-C. The rebuttal numbers had no error bars, and its summary claim that 2-OPT-C 'substantially outperforms benchmarks in all of these problems' conflicts with its own ties with PESC (robot pushing) and ADMMBO (P3 at 60 evaluations). No reviewer remarked on this.

ac.evidence: Mean 6.25, three of four ratings above threshold. The meta-review says the reviewers reached a 'consensus' that the paper 'offered a significant contribution', and that they 'agree' the portfolio example 'was both relevant and convincing'. That overstates the panel: 8KpE stayed at 5 and questioned the portfolio set-up, and uDRU's text still says the paper cannot be accepted as written. The note adds no technical judgment of its own.

main_reasons_for_decision: The rebuttal's portfolio experiment moved HPhn from 6 to 7 and Strq up to 7, giving the paper two champions
uDRU rose to 6 for the volume of rebuttal work, despite unresolved clarity complaints and misreadings
The AC read the panel as a consensus and made the portfolio example a condition for the camera-ready

issues_only_a: More baselines: random search, Thompson sampling, IECI [25] and the other cited constrained BO methods (iK1S, vkHd)
Claim of better query efficiency than rollout in high dimensions has no experiment (wxwg; lines 65-67)
Novelty claim at lines 220-221, first likelihood-ratio gradient estimator in BO, contested via [17] Section 3.2 (iK1S)
Weak motivation: applications only named in passing at lines 26-27 (vkHd)
Equality constraints, failures and binary constraints not handled (iK1S)
Myopia framing ignores UCB and Thompson sampling (vkHd; a misreading of lines 37-38)
Number of replications not in the main text (F2Td)
issues_only_b: Clarity and self-containedness: non-myopia, IPA and SAA not formally defined; Assumption 1 only in the supplement (uDRU)
No test that non-myopia causes the gain; a modified EIC that explores infeasible points might match it (8KpE)
Costly or unsafe infeasible evaluations would favour EIC (8KpE)
Theorem 1 needs delta > 0, which may exclude the optimum (8KpE)
Links to other multi-step methods (Jiang et al. 2020, Lee et al. 2020) and missing multi-step references (HPhn, 8KpE)
Portfolio problem: constraint level and relation to BO of risk measures (8KpE, post-rebuttal)
Reacting-flow problem P4 of [1] not tested (Strq)
shared_issues: Evaluation limited to three synthetic problems from [1], with no real-world problem (all four A reviewers; Strq and 8KpE in B)
Incremental over Wu & Frazier 2019 [17] (iK1S in A; HPhn in B)
Second stage evaluates one point, not a batch (iK1S in A; 8KpE and uDRU in B)
Rollout comparison relies on numbers copied from [1] (vkHd in A; uDRU in B)
Computational cost against other methods only discussed indirectly in the main paper (F2Td in A; 8KpE in B)
verdict: Both committees judged the same weakness and received the same rebuttal; they differed on whether rebuttal-period experiments count. The submission tests 2-OPT-C on three synthetic problems from Lam & Willcox [1], against two myopic baselines, with rollout curves copied from [1] (lines 269-293). Six of the eight reviewers called the evaluation thin (all four in A; Reviewer_Strq and Reviewer_8KpE in B), and the paper confirms it. In both forums the authors posted a portfolio-optimization experiment on 2021-08-10/11, then robot pushing and four more baselines (ADMMBO, NEI, ALBO, random search) on 2021-09-01/02. In B, the portfolio result moved Reviewer_HPhn from 6 to 7 and Reviewer_Strq up to 7 within about two weeks, and Reviewer_uDRU rose to 6, 'impressed by the amount of work'. In A, only Reviewer_wxwg moved, from 4 or lower to 5, citing clarifications. A's two 6s never edited: Reviewer_iK1S (confidence 5) and Reviewer_F2Td, whose 'only concern' was real-world experiments. So A had no champion and B had two. A's AC copied Reviewer_vkHd's demand for '1-3 real benchmarks ..., more baselines, and ablation studies' and named no rebuttal result. B's AC called the panel a consensus and accepted on the portfolio example. B's case is weaker than its mean suggests. Its three raisers spent 2 to 3 hours each, uDRU misread the method twice, and the most thorough B reviewer, Reviewer_8KpE (about 6 hours), stayed at 5. The rebuttal numbers had no error bars, and its summary called ties with PESC and ADMMBO wins. A's case is weaker than its decision suggests: three of its four reviewers did not react to evidence that answered their main request, and the camera-ready contains the new problems and baselines. No reviewer found a technical error. Before the rebuttal no rating in either panel was above 6; the split in means (6.25 against 5.25) opened in the rebuttal phase.
